title: Did Jensen Huang Fool Everyone? A Black Swan Looms and This Year’s Biggest AI Stock Surprise Isn’t TSMC
gist: Short SemiWiki forum teaser for a CommonWealth (cwnewsroom) interview with former UBS semiconductor analyst Jonah Cheng ('Captain'), who flags the November U.S. midterms as an AI black swan, warns record CSP GPU inventories plus power shortages could force a correction, questions the industry chase toward 7-9x reticle packages versus Nvidia's 5.5x Rubin Ultra, values MediaTek's TPU role for SerDes IP, and names Largan Precision (optical communications) as 2026's biggest AI stock surprise. The post only previews the calls; the underlying reasoning is not included.

insights.claim: Former UBS semiconductor analyst Jonah Cheng ('Captain') sees the November U.S. midterm elections, rather than an AI bubble, as the biggest black-swan risk to the AI boom.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Treat the November midterms as an event-risk window for AI semiconductor positioning and hedging.
insights.quote: What if the biggest risk to the AI boom isn’t an AI bubble at all?

insights.claim: Cloud service providers are still racing to buy GPUs even as GPU inventories sit at record highs, per Jonah Cheng.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Record channel/customer inventory alongside continued buying is a classic late-cycle signal; monitor CSP inventory and capex guidance.
insights.quote: CSPs are still racing to buy GPUs even as inventories hit record highs

insights.claim: Jonah Cheng argues a power shortage could prevent deployment of stockpiled GPUs and eventually turn the CSP inventory buildup into a painful correction for the AI hardware supply chain.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Power availability is a binding constraint to watch; data-center power delays could translate into GPU order cuts.
insights.quote: a power shortage could eventually turn that buildup into a painful correction

insights.claim: Google and others are pushing toward 7x, 8x and 9x reticle-size packages while Nvidia has stopped at 5.5x reticle with Rubin Ultra, and Jonah Cheng questions whether the industry is chasing the wrong target.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: If oversized packages prove the wrong bet, suppliers levered to 7-9x reticle packaging roadmaps face execution/demand risk; Nvidia's more conservative choice may be the safer path.
insights.quote: Did Jensen Huang’s Rubin Ultra roadmap send everyone chasing the wrong target?

insights.claim: Jonah Cheng argues MediaTek's real value in Google's TPU supply chain is its SerDes IP, which Google cannot easily replicate, rather than its low-margin design services.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: SerDes IP gives MediaTek a stickier moat in custom ASIC programs than design-service margins imply, supporting its position in Google TPU work.
insights.quote: its real value in Google’s TPU supply chain isn’t low-margin design services, but something Google cannot easily replicate: SerDes IP

insights.claim: Jonah Cheng names Largan Precision, not TSMC, as the biggest AI stock surprise of 2026, citing its unexpected emergence as a serious player in optical communications.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Largan is flagged as an under-the-radar AI optical-communications beneficiary; watch for evidence of its traction in optical communications.
insights.quote: Largan Precision—a company few expected to emerge as a serious player in optical communications
